transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time today. It's probably nothing major, but... well, lately my head just feels a little cloudy. 

I feel a bit silly even saying it out loud, to be honest. But I'll be sitting at my desk, staring at a board packet for the properties I manage, or just looking at a regular email from a vendor, and I just... I can't seem to decide on even the simple things. Things I used to handle real fast without a second thought. 

I don't know, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in, and I hope it's okay that I'm bothering you with this.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't really say sad. I mean, I hope I don't sound like I'm complaining about my life, because I know I have a whole lot to be grateful for. 

It's mostly just that... well, that foggy feeling I was talking about. I don't really feel down in the dumps or anything like that. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about anything lately?

Anxious? Um... no, not really. I mean, I worry a little bit about doing a good job at work, just making sure the properties are taken care of and the residents are happy. But that's just normal, right? I think everyone worries about their job a little. 

I'm definitely not, like, a nervous wreck or anything. I hope it's alright that I don't have a better answer for you. I just... I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing. Am I explaining this okay?
Have you been having trouble focusing or concentrating on things lately?

Yes, I think that's exactly it. Um, like I was mentioning earlier... it's just that cloudy feeling. I'll be looking right at a vendor email, or one of those board packets, and my brain just sort of... stalls out, I guess? 

I just can't seem to concentrate enough to make a simple choice on things I used to handle real fast. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Does that sound like what you mean by trouble focusing?
Have you been having any trouble with your memory lately?

Memory? Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I might misplace my keys every now and then, or forget why I walked into the kitchen, but at my age, I figure that's just part of getting older, right? 

I haven't forgotten any big things, like paying the bills or important dates. My memory seems pretty normal, I think. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering these questions the way you need me to.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?

Tired? Well, um... no, I wouldn't say more than usual. I mean, sure, by the time the evening rolls around I'm ready to sit down, especially if I had to walk the grounds at one of the properties. But I think anyone my age gets a little worn out after a full day of work, right? 

I'm certainly not laying in bed all day or anything bad like that. I still get up and do what I need to do every morning with plenty of energy. I hope that's okay? I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you a good picture of how I'm doing. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you been feeling irritable lately?

Irritable? Oh, my... well, I really try so hard to be pleasant with everyone, you know? I don't want you to think I'm a difficult person. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest... maybe a little bit? 

I feel awful even admitting it. It's just... there were a few days recently where I felt almost, um, too bright and bold, I guess you could say. I'd be running the association meetings and I'd catch myself just talking right over people. Which really isn't like me at all! And then I'd get home and... well, I'd end up snapping at my husband over some tiny little thing. 

I always make sure to apologize right away, of course, because I hate being short with him. I hope it's alright that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Enjoying things? Oh, well... I mean, I try to. I really do try to keep up with everything. I know it's important to stay active. But... um... 

Well, lately... I suppose I haven't been doing my usual activities as much as I should. I feel terrible even saying it, because I know my family looks forward to it, but I just haven't had the desire to cook our big Sunday dinners recently. And... well, I usually love going to my dance class and walking through the little art galleries in town. Those are the things that usually make me feel like myself, you know? But lately, I just... haven't wanted to go. 

I know I should, and I'm going to try to get back to it soon, I promise. I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up or being lazy. Is it okay that I'm sharing that with you? I hope I'm not sounding too negative... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future?

Hopeless? Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say hopeless. I mean, I know things can get a little... overwhelming sometimes, but I always try to look on the bright side, you know? 

I really believe things will get better. I mean, they have to, right? I have my husband, and the properties to manage, and... well, I just try to keep a positive attitude about everything. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. That's not me at all. 

I hope that makes sense? I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I'm looking at things. I'm really trying my best to stay optimistic. Is that... is that a good way to look at it?
Do you find that you worry about the same things over and over?

Worry about the same things? Oh, I... well, I suppose everyone worries a little bit, don't they? I mean, with managing the properties and making sure everything is running smoothly, there's always something to keep an eye on. 

But I wouldn't say I worry about the *same* things over and over. Not to the point where it's a problem or anything like that. I really try to just handle whatever comes up and move on. I don't want to be one of those people who just frets all day long. I try to be very capable, you know? 

I hope I'm answering that right? I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around making myself sick with worry. I really do try to handle things well. Does that sound okay to you?
Do you find yourself preoccupied with certain thoughts that you can't seem to shake off?

Preoccupied? Oh, um... well, no, I don't think so. I mean, my mind stays pretty busy, of course, with the properties and making sure the tenants are happy and all the maintenance is scheduled. You have to stay on top of those things, you know? 

But I wouldn't say I'm preoccupied in a bad way, or stuck on things I can't shake off. I try very hard to just deal with a problem when it comes up and then put it out of my mind. I don't like to dwell on things. I think it's so much healthier to just keep moving forward, don't you? 

I really try to keep my thoughts productive. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Oh, goodness, no. I really don't think I do that. I mean, if I'm ever concerned about something, there's always a real reason for it, like a plumbing issue at one of the units or a contractor running late. 

I wouldn't just sit around worrying about... well, nothing. That just seems like a silly waste of energy, doesn't it? I always try to be very practical. If there's no obvious reason to fret, I just go about my day and focus on what needs to get done. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just imagines problems out of thin air. I try to be very sensible about it all. 

I hope that's the right way to handle things? I just want to be sure I'm doing okay.
Do you find yourself worrying about things more days than not?

More days than not? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, sure, there are days when the phone is ringing off the hook and a tenant has a leaky roof, and I might feel a little... well, a little tense, just wanting to make sure it all gets sorted out. 

But most days? No, most days I'm just busy getting things done. I try to keep a very positive attitude. I think if you go around worrying most of the week, it just drags you down, and I really try my best not to let that happen. I want to be someone who handles her responsibilities with a smile, you know? 

I hope that makes sense? I just really want to be clear that I'm managing things well. Is that... is that a good sign, do you think?
Have you noticed a decrease in the pleasure you get from activities you normally enjoy?

Well, um... I suppose, maybe just a little bit lately? But it's probably just because I've been so busy with the properties, you know? 

I mean, usually, I just love going to my dance class, and I always enjoy strolling through the little art galleries downtown. And cooking a big Sunday dinner for my family—oh, that’s always been something that makes me feel so... so much like myself. But recently, I just haven't really had the desire to do those things. I've been skipping the class and ordering takeout on Sundays instead. 

I feel a little guilty about it, honestly. I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies and my family. I just... I haven't quite felt up to it. But I'm sure it's just a phase, right? Everyone gets a little tired sometimes. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy? I really do plan to get back to it all very soon.
How long have you been feeling this cloudy and having trouble concentrating?

Well, um... I guess this really noticeable shift—you know, where I first had that burst of energy and felt like I could take on the world, and then suddenly dropped into this... this low, cloudy sort of fog—it's been about two weeks now. 

It started right around the time my husband retired. Suddenly he was just... home all day, every day. It’s been a bit of an adjustment, I suppose. I mean, I love having him around, of course! I don't want to sound like a terrible wife complaining about her husband. It's just... a big change to our routine, and maybe I haven't handled the transition as perfectly as I should have. 

Two weeks isn't that long though, right? I'm hoping I'll bounce back and get my focus back soon. I really am trying my best to push through it. Do you think that's a normal reaction to such a big life change?
Have you been feeling a lack of interest or pleasure in your daily activities most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, um... I guess I sort of mentioned this a minute ago, but... yes, I suppose it has been most of the day, nearly every day lately. 

Like I said, I just haven't wanted to go to my dance class at all, or even just take a walk to look at the little galleries downtown. And the Sunday dinners... I haven't cooked one in a couple of weeks. Those are the things that usually make me feel so much like myself, you know? And lately, I just... I wake up and the thought of doing them just feels like too much. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm just giving up or being ungrateful for the nice things in my life. I know I should be making more of an effort. I just... I haven't been able to muster up the enthusiasm. I'm trying not to let it show too much around my husband, especially now that he's home. I want to be a good partner to him. 

Is it... is it okay that I'm feeling this way right now? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something wrong by taking a little step back from my hobbies.
How long have you been feeling a lack of interest or pleasure in your daily activities?

Well, um... to be completely honest with you, I suppose these sort of... depressed stretches... they've actually been coming back on and off for about a year now. I didn't want to make a big fuss over it before, because usually I can just put on a smile and get my work done with the properties. I didn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle things, you know? 

But this latest one... it really feels more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working. It just sort of settled in heavier this time, and I haven't been able to shake it off as easily. 

I hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses or complaining about my life? A year sounds like a long time when I say it out loud, but I promise I usually manage it much better than this. Does that make sense, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

Well, um... I guess I sort of am feeling that way most of the day, yes. 

I mean, I try to put a brave face on, especially for my husband. I don't want him to think his retirement is making me miserable or anything! I really do try to stay upbeat and keep busy with the properties when I can. But... if I'm being perfectly honest, even when I'm smiling, there's just this heavy, sad feeling sitting right there underneath it all, pretty much from the time I wake up until I go to sleep.

I know I shouldn't be letting it get to me this much. I have a wonderful life and a lot to be thankful for. I just... I haven't been able to snap out of it lately. Do you think it's terrible that I can't just be happy right now? I really am trying to be positive, I promise.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately?

Well, um... I haven't actually been stepping on the scale much, so I don't have an exact number for you. I hope that's alright, I know I should probably keep better track of things like that for my health. 

But I guess... well, my eating has been a little off lately. Please don't think I'm not taking care of myself! It's just that during the day, a cup of coffee and just a few little bites seem to carry me through most of the afternoon. And then at night, I mostly just pick at some tortillas or maybe a few sweets, even though I'm not really enjoying them the way I normally would. 

I'm still making sure I eat something, I promise. Is it normal to just lose your appetite a bit when you're feeling this way? I just want to make sure I'm not doing any harm by not having full meals right now.
